sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who sets the value
sections.html:
Two separate offices split the work. The Bartow County Tax Commissioner mails and collects the bill. A Board of Tax Assessors puts the value on your land and house. Payments, mobile home accounts and tax sale overage claims all go to the commissioner's suite in the Frank Moore Administration and Judicial Building, 135 W. Cherokee Avenue, Suite 217A, Cartersville. Call the property tax line at (770) 387-5111. The counter is open Monday through Friday, eight in the morning until five, except holidays.

Bartow has a sole commissioner form of government. One elected commissioner approves the budget and sets the millage at a public meeting in that same building. Cartersville is the county seat. Adairsville, Euharlee, Kingston and Taylorsville have their own charters, while Cassville, Rydal and Allatoona are unincorporated communities that still pay through the county office.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, duplicate bills, excess funds forms
  • Board of Tax Assessors: values, returns and the notices that carry appeal rights
  • County Commissioner: sets the rates and the budget each summer

sections.h2: Bartow County for a home seller
sections.html:
The county sits in northwest Georgia, and the Cartersville end of it now behaves like an Atlanta exurb, reached by I-75. Population moved from 100,157 in 2010 to 108,901 in 2020, with an estimate of 120,800 for mid-2025. A large industrial base, a battery plant and data center development have lifted the tax digest, and that growth has let the millage keep falling.

The housing count is 50,010 units in 2025, with 72.8 percent of households owning. The middle owner-occupied value is $289,000, middle rent is $1,268 a month and middle household income is $82,243. A house in Cartersville falls under Cartersville City Schools, while most other addresses belong to the Bartow County School District, so confirm the district before you describe a listing to a buyer.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Statements for real estate leave the office around September 15, and the bill is due November 15. Mobile homes follow their own cycle with an April 1 due date.

Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 is the billed party. If you closed on a purchase after that date, phone the tax office and ask for a duplicate in your name, because the first statement went to the previous owner. A bill that never arrives does not move the deadline.

  • Online payment sits behind a link on the Tax Commissioner page, and the same page lists qpublic for parcel lookups
  • Debit and credit cards, whether paid online, at the counter or by phone, add a 2.5 percent convenience charge
  • A check by mail is made out to the Bartow County Tax Commissioner at the Cherokee Avenue address

Georgia gives every taxpayer 60 days from the postmark on the bill before interest starts, and delinquent balances can also draw penalties. Ask the office for the figure that applies to your account.

The 2026 rate is 7.11 mills inside city limits and 6.76 mills in the unincorporated county, down from 7.40 and 6.87 the year before. The commissioner chose the rollback rate, and rates have trended down since 2013.

A mill is a dollar of tax on each $1,000 of assessed value, and assessed value is set at 40 percent of fair market value. The school board levies its own rate on top, so your statement shows more than the county figure alone. Ask the tax office for the combined millage tied to your parcel and district.

File with the county before April 1, and only for the home where you live. Rentals, multi-family buildings and commercial or industrial property are excluded.

The standard exemption is $15,000 of value. County leaders are working with the legislature on a move to $30,000 in a future year, but that has not happened yet, so call the office to learn the amount on your current bill. Moving to another Bartow house means filing again for the new address. A buyer of your house must apply too, because your exemption does not transfer.

Mail a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked no later than 45 days after the notice date. Georgia sets that window for every county, and it covers disputes about fair market value.

Before any notice arrives, owners may file a return between January 1 and April 1 stating the value they believe is right. Money paid on tax that was wrongly charged can be claimed back within three years of payment, and refunds from a winning appeal are issued automatically. Gather sale prices of nearby houses and dated photos of any damage before you write the appeal.

The unpaid tax rides with the property, so closing is the moment to settle it. Because the county names the January 1 owner, a seller who held title on that day normally gets the statement even if the deed changes hands in October. Ask whoever handles your closing to show how the year's bill is split and who sends the payment.

When back taxes pile up and the county sells the parcel for more than is owed, the excess is held for the people with a claim. The commissioner's page links an excess funds form for that situation. Selling before a levy usually costs less than waiting, so request a written payoff from the office and compare it with any offer you receive.

Here is how the work usually runs:

  1. Phone (770) 387-5111 and ask for the balance and the billed owner.
  2. If a lender escrows your tax, ask the servicer whether this year's bill has been paid.
  3. Give the title company the written payoff.
  4. Have the closing statement show who covers which part of the year.

A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can close without repair demands. Back taxes are still cleared from your proceeds, so the payoff is worth requesting early.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Bartow County?
faqs.a: November 15, with statements mailed around September 15. Mobile home bills are due April 1.

faqs.q: What is the last day to apply for homestead in Bartow County?
faqs.a: April 1. The exemption only covers the home you live in as a primary residence.

faqs.q: How many days do I get to appeal a Bartow assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the notice was mailed. Postmark the written appeal inside that window and send it to the Board of Tax Assessors.

faqs.q: Will Bartow County send my bill to the lender?
faqs.a: No. Statements go to whoever held title on January 1, so ask your lender whether it pays from escrow. A buyer who closed after January 1 can call (770) 387-5111 for a duplicate statement.

faqs.q: Does Bartow County charge a fee to pay by card?
faqs.a: Yes, 2.5 percent on debit and credit payments, whether made online, in person or by phone. A check by mail carries no such fee.
